answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted rate limiting with decaying reputation. Every agent locks a small refundable deposit before transacting; the deposit is nectar that rewards honest work but is costly to fake at scale. New identities start with tight quotas that widen only as dispute-free interactions accumulate, a juniper-slow growth that sybils cannot rush. If requests wander into spammy patterns, peers slash the quota and burn part of the deposit, so manufacturing thousands of fake identities costs real money while honest agents earn limits back.
